## 17 call sites still pass the legacy rounding flag

`src/reports/quarterly.js` has the most, with **5**.

| File | 2-arg calls | (of total `formatAmount` calls) |
|---|---|---|
| `src/reports/quarterly.js` | **5** | 31 |
| `src/admin/exports.js` | 3 | 21 |
| `src/billing/invoice.js` | 3 | 26 |
| `src/checkout/cart.js` | 2 | 23 |
| `src/reports/monthly.js` | 2 | 24 |
| `src/billing/statement.js` | 1 | 22 |
| `src/checkout/receipt.js` | 1 | 18 |
| `src/admin/dashboard.js` | 0 | 17 |
| `src/billing/refunds.js` | 0 | 19 |
| `src/reports/ledger.js` | 0 | 20 |

Total: 221 call sites across 10 files, 17 of which pass the second argument.

The sites:

```
src/admin/exports.js:16      formatAmount(row.tip, true)
src/admin/exports.js:37      formatAmount(row.commission, true)
src/admin/exports.js:62      formatAmount(row.credit, true)
src/billing/invoice.js:16    formatAmount(row.tip, true)
src/billing/invoice.js:45    formatAmount(row.balance, true)
src/billing/invoice.js:74    formatAmount(row.payout, true)
src/billing/statement.js:16  formatAmount(row.bundle, true)
src/checkout/cart.js:16      formatAmount(row.prepayment, true)
src/checkout/cart.js:53      formatAmount(row.writeOff, true)
src/checkout/receipt.js:16   formatAmount(row.tip, true)
src/reports/monthly.js:16    formatAmount(row.tip, true)
src/reports/monthly.js:57    formatAmount(row.settlement, true)
src/reports/quarterly.js:16  formatAmount(row.bundle, true)
src/reports/quarterly.js:37  formatAmount(row.holdback, true)
src/reports/quarterly.js:58  formatAmount(row.subtotal, true)
src/reports/quarterly.js:83  formatAmount(row.surcharge, true)
src/reports/quarterly.js:104 formatAmount(row.gross, true)
```

Notes on the sweep:

- I counted arguments with a real paren-matching parse (comments and string literals blanked out first) rather than a line regex, so nested calls like `formatAmount(f(a, b))` couldn't inflate the count. In practice every call turned out to be a single-line, flat expression.
- All 17 pass the literal `true` — there are no variable or computed flags, so each site is an unconditional legacy-rounding request. That makes the removal mechanical: delete the argument and accept the behavior change from half-away-from-zero to half-to-even.
- No indirect paths to worry about: no aliased imports, no `.call`/`.apply`/`.bind`, no spread arguments, and the only non-call mentions are the 10 `require` destructures plus the definition and export in `src/lib/format.js`. The repo is 11 JS files under `src/` plus one JSON file that doesn't reference the function.
- The one thing that changes behavior beyond the flag itself: these 17 sites are the only ones whose output will move, and only for values landing exactly on a half-cent boundary.
